overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the two-member communications at the July 30 training and the October 15 texts were subquorum, and the quick vote alone did not show outside deliberation.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged members deliberated about the school mascot at a July 30 anti-bias training that was not open to the public, with a quorum present.
allegations.key_passage: We find that such communication did not constitute deliberation because the communication was between two members of the Committee, which is not a quorum.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged members deliberated by text message during the October 15 meeting about retiring the mascot, including a chair-to-member text.
allegations.key_passage: we find that it did not constitute deliberation outside of a posted meeting and therefore did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint argued the lack of substantive discussion and the quick vote to retire the mascot showed members had deliberated outside a noticed meeting.
allegations.key_passage: agreement without substantive discussion among public body members or even the lack of substantive discussion prior to a vote is insufficient to support the inference that those members deliberated outside of a noticed meeting.
